headline: Kospi plunges 8%, trading halted: Why South Korean market is seeing extreme volatility - BusinessToday
summary: South Korea's Kospi has swung sharply in recent sessions, with trading halted after a steep 8% fall. Concerns over leveraged funds linked to newly introduced blue-chip stock products are believed to have amplified volatility.
why: The Kospi is South Korea's main stock benchmark, dominated by large exporters such as Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix. Its swings affect global risk sentiment and Asian equity flows.

impacts.name: Kospi
impacts.why: The benchmark index fell 8% and trading was halted during extreme volatility.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Leveraged funds tied to blue-chip stocks, introduced last month, are believed to have amplified the market's volatility, according to the report.
